claims.text: Phase stability in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed by a critical undercooling.
Crossing the critical undercooling triggers local Al segregation.
Local Al segregation produces short-range chemical ordering.
The short-range chemical ordering relieves elastic strain.
The short-range chemical ordering lowers the free-energy barrier for phase transformation.
Lowering this barrier enables transformation of the high-temperature BCC state into a secondary phase, potentially incipient FCC or mixed phases.
The initial Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 alloy is a homogeneous high-temperature BCC phase.
Annealing below the critical threshold provides sufficient undercooling to drive local Al clustering and chemical ordering.
At slightly higher temperatures, kinetic suppression delays Al segregation and preserves the high-temperature BCC phase.
A sample annealed at approximately 900 °C will develop secondary-phase nucleation signatures in diffraction.
A sample annealed at approximately 900 °C will develop observable Al-enriched regions.
A sample annealed at approximately 950 °C will remain predominantly homogeneous and BCC.
A sample annealed at approximately 950 °C will show minimal Al segregation.
Standard high-temperature processing without pre-anneal homogenization or temperature adjustment maintains a metastable BCC configuration in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
The proposed phase-stability mechanism may not apply under mechanical deformation or vastly different cooling rates.
